item.problem: Overstated and inconsistent with the lesson's own point that insects are small and the grasshopper's haemolymph does not carry oxygen; also 'delivering 20+ litres of oxygenated blood per minute' conflates blood with oxygen; cardiac output in elite athletes is about 30-40 L/min so figure is fine, but claim that muscles fail within seconds due to the circulatory system is unsupported.
item.quote_a: his muscles would fail within seconds of any intense effort
item.correct_value: Muscles could not receive enough oxygen via diffusion/haemolymph to sustain aerobic effort

items.recommendation: Replace the unsupported 'fail within seconds' claim with a mechanistic statement consistent with Lesson 3.
items.reason: The 'within seconds' claim is unsupported by the plan; the lesson's own evidence is about oxygen delivery capacity, not timing.

edit.old: his muscles would fail within seconds of any intense effort
edit.new: his muscles could not receive enough oxygen to sustain aerobic effort, because a low-pressure open system cannot direct oxygen-carrying fluid to working muscles on demand

items.reference: Insects use tracheae for gas exchange; haemolymph does not carry O2 (Lesson 3); closed circulation delivers O2 via haemoglobin-rich blood.
